name: Phase I environmental site assessment
what: An environmental professional's report on whether the property shows signs of contamination, based on records, interviews and a site visit.

fields.label: Standard
fields.definition: The practice the report follows: ASTM E1527-21, or E2247-23 for forestland or rural property.

fields.label: Environmental professional
fields.definition: The person who signed the report's declaration, with the qualifications the report states.

fields.label: Site visit
fields.definition: The date of the visual inspection of the property and adjoining properties.

fields.label: Earliest 180-day component
fields.definition: The earliest of the interviews, cleanup-lien search, government records review, site visit and declaration; acquisition must follow within 180 days of it.

fields.label: Inquiry date
fields.definition: When the inquiry was conducted; acquisition must follow within one year.

fields.label: Conditions found
fields.definition: Conditions the professional identified as indicating releases or threatened releases of hazardous substances, which ASTM reports call recognized environmental conditions.

fields.label: Data gaps
fields.definition: Information the professional could not obtain, with comments on how much each gap matters.

fields.label: Further investigation
fields.definition: The professional's opinion on additional appropriate investigation, such as a Phase II, if it has one.

fields.label: Buyer's own inquiries
fields.definition: The buyer's cleanup-lien search, specialized knowledge and comparison of price with uncontaminated value.
